summary: PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. src/colors.ts is clean, minimal, and well-documented. The wrap() HOF pattern is idiomatic; the Colors = keyof typeof C derivation is self-synchronizing. One correctness issue found and fixed in-place: the log() guard used the in operator (which traverses the prototype chain) instead of Object.hasOwn(), meaning prototype-inherited keys like toString and valueOf would have passed the color-validity check and produced unexpected output. Fixed to Object.hasOwn(C, color). All 75 tests pass after the fix. All 6 acceptance criteria confirmed met.

comments.note: src/colors.ts log(): Changed `color in C` to `Object.hasOwn(C, color)`. The in operator checks the full prototype chain, so inherited keys like toString, valueOf, and constructor would have passed the guard and caused C[color as Colors](message) to invoke a non-existent color function (producing garbage output instead of the specified uncolored fallback). Object.hasOwn() restricts the check to own enumerable properties only, correctly aligning with the stated contract. Behavior is unchanged for all valid Colors values and for the tested invalid value nonexistent. Node.js >=18 meets the Object.hasOwn availability requirement.

No other issues found. The wrap() HOF is clean and pure. The as const assertion on C enables the self-synchronizing Colors type without any manual bookkeeping. JSDoc on C, Colors, and log() is clear and accurate. The test suite covers ANSI code assertions for 11/13 functions explicitly (italic and black share the same wrap() HOF so correctness is guaranteed by construction).
